data.cultural_impact: The name Jesse holds great significance in Judeo-Christian culture due to its biblical origins. In the Old Testament book of Samuel, Jesse is depicted as a shepherd king of the tribe of Judah. He is described as a mighty man of valor, and he is also the father of King David, who is considered one of the greatest kings in Jewish and Christian history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jesse carries a profound spiritual meaning, highlighting the idea that all of us are God's gifts to the world. In the biblical narrative, Jesse is chosen by God to be the father of King David, who is anointed as the future king of Israel. This suggests that even the most seemingly insignificant individuals can be used by God to accomplish great things.

historical_references.reference: The Old Testament prophecy in Isaiah 11:1 refers to a future king of Israel whose lineage is traced back to Jesse, the father of King David. This prophecy was believed to have been written around the 8th century BC.
The New Testament names Jesus as the descendant of Jesse, as recorded in Matthew 1:6 and Luke 3:32. Jesus' genealogy is traced back to Abraham, then to Jesse, and ultimately to King David.
